A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same MOMEMTO research work. Their complete main text and appendices are readable, and corresponding equations, tables and figures can be matched despite pagination changes.

before.justification: V1 reports original benchmark evaluations, component ablations, few-shot and zero-shot experiments, memory-utilization analyses, and computational measurements in Section 4 and Appendix C.

after.justification: V2 retains these empirical results and adds memory-capacity sensitivity experiments in Appendix C.4.

M1.justification: The architecture and gated memory mechanism are retained; the newly named query-alignment stage elaborates existing concatenation. However, Algorithm 1 now normalizes q in place before concatenation, whereas v1 preserves the original q. Algorithm 2 inconsistently retains a reference to q-hat. The PDFs do not resolve whether this represents a procedural change or a notation error.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same TSB-AD-U coverage, including the 350-series evaluation set grouped into 32 domains. Few-shot and held-out-domain zero-shot evaluations already appear in v1. The new memory-capacity study introduces no new dataset or task.

E2.justification: Table 1 adds evaluated KAN-AD and DADA baselines while retaining all 13 previous comparators, although the prose still says 13 baselines. Comparator membership in the domain-level and zero-shot tables remains unchanged.

E3.justification: New Appendix C.4 varies total memory capacity from 64 to 1 using K-means-centroid initialization and evaluates several capacities across existing training-data ratios. These are protocols for added experiments; the previously reported splits, metrics, window sizes and training budgets remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Appendix C.4 adds a focused sensitivity analysis of total memory capacity, with full-data and few-shot results in Tables 11–12 and beginning-versus-end training heatmaps in Figure 6. This differs from the retained Appendix C.3 analysis of how many memory items are retrieved.

E5.justification: Neither version reports experimental run counts, seeds, confidence intervals or significance tests. The added tables continue point-estimate reporting, and existing plots retain their reporting practices.

E6.justification: Existing numerical results are retained. Table 1 adds KAN-AD and DADA scores; DADA's AUC-PR of 33.59 exceeds per-dataset MOMEMTO's 32.83, while multi-domain MOMEMTO remains highest at 36.35. New Tables 11–12 report memory-capacity results, including full-data AUC-PR values of 35.69–36.26 under K-means initialization.

T1.justification: No new theoretical assumptions, propositions, proofs or independent derivations appear. The added main-text gate and attention equations elaborate operations already described in v1's Appendix B.4, while the weighted query combination is rewritten in summation notation.

C1.justification: The abstract and introduction recast MOMEMTO as an improved MOMENT variant. The contribution claiming the first TFM specialized in anomaly detection becomes a claim about extending MOMENT. The central memory, multi-domain training and empirical performance claims remain.

C2.justification: V2 adds interpretations of stable performance across memory capacities and reliance on a small subset of memory items. It also explains positional preservation through query alignment and attributes interval/periodic-anomaly weaknesses to MEMTO's point-level memory. The univariate-evaluation and missing-theory limitations remain unchanged.

D1.justification: Appendix C.4 documents K-means-centroid initialization and the configurations used for the new sensitivity study. Existing hardware and hyperparameter disclosures remain unchanged. Table 7 is not extended with settings for the newly added baselines.

R1.justification: V2 adds the KAN-AD and DADA references and positions MOMEMTO more explicitly as a MOMENT extension. The introduction adds a MEMTO limitation supported by the already cited Shen work; the related-work section otherwise retains its coverage.

P1.justification: The abstract and introduction receive limited rewrites, and Section 3.1.2 expands its explanation into five named stages with revised notation. A new Appendix C.4 shifts the anomaly-score appendix to C.5. The overall narrative and section order remain stable.

P2.justification: Table 1 gains two rows, and v2 adds Tables 11–12 and a four-panel Figure 6. Table 3 and Figure 4 move, with Figure 4's caption clarified. All carried-over figure images are unchanged, including the former appendix Figure 6, now Figure 7.

improvement.justification: V2 modestly strengthens the paper through two additional evaluated comparators, targeted evidence about memory capacity, and more precise positioning as a MOMENT extension. Documentation remains uneven: the added baselines lack hyperparameters in Table 7, and revised query notation leaves procedural ambiguity. These limitations temper, but do not outweigh, the added evidence and clearer contribution framing.
